subject: Private DNS & certificate consolidation for hybrid VPC: egress policy and termination options
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: SRE Team <sre@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private DNS & cert consolidation — kickoff and questions

Hi Jake / Acme SRE,

Thanks for taking the meeting yesterday. Per our discussion, we sketched two high-level goals for the private deployment: (1) reduce operational overhead for certificates across multi-AZ VPCs, and (2) preserve Acme's egress and audit controls (no unexpected outbound TLS termination outside your network).

Attached is a quick diagram (acme_mtls_diagram.png) and a short consolidation proposal (consolidation_proposal_v1.pdf) with three options at a glance. Before we dig into an implementation plan we need a few clarifying items from your side so our engineering/design team can produce a clean runbook:

- Which DNS resolvers are authoritative for the private domain (names and whether they are forwarders vs. authoritative)?
- Do you require CRL/OCSP stapling checks to happen on-prem (no external queries)?
- Are you willing to accept a Redwood-managed cert issued from your internal CA (we can support cross-signed chain provisioning) or must the certs be generated and stored only within your KMS/HSM?
- Any TLS inspection/proxying appliances in the egress path we should be aware of (vendor & model)?

Our ask: can you provide a minimal answers doc and a zone-file or resolver IPs by EOD Monday? We want to avoid multiple back-and-forths during the pilot.

Best,
Ben Carter

From: Jake Torres <jake.torres@acme-corp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@acme-corp.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:45:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Private DNS & cert consolidation — kickoff and questions

Ben — thanks, diagram and summary look useful. Quick answers inline: 

- Authoritative: ns1.internal.acme (10.11.0.5), ns2.internal.acme (10.11.0.6). We use an internal bind cluster; they are authoritative and also forward to our central resolver for Internet names.
- OCSP/CRL: Must be satisfied without egress to public OCSP endpoints. If OCSP stapling is used we need to verify stapled responses come from a trusted Redwood responder or the cert must include locally verifiable validity windows.
- CA policy: We prefer certs generated and stored inside our HSM/KMS. However, we can consider cross-signed certs if Redwood can present an auditable key provisioning flow (KMS wrap/unwrap logs) and we can perform periodic key attestations.
- TLS inspection: We have an egress TLS proxy (BlueSentinel TS-400) that does SNI allow-listing and cert pinning for outbound services. It will reject connections where SNI doesn't map to an allowed FQDN or where the cert chain validation fails.

Constraints/timeline: any solution that requires outbound validation to public OCSP URLs will be a blocker for our security review. We aim to close the pilot scope by June 10 given procurement windows.

Jake Torres
SRE Lead — Acme Cloud Retail
sre@acme-corp.com

Jake — great, thanks for the quick clarifications. Looping in Karthik and Marissa to map options to our product constraints. Below are three proposals with the pros/cons and what we need from Acme to proceed. Please call out any hard blockers.

Option A — Redwood-terminates in-customer VPC (private peering):
- Model: Redwood runtime in Acme VPC (dedicated host), we terminate TLS at an internal load balancer under Acme account but with certs provisioned by Redwood and cross-signed by your CA.
- Pros: unified cert lifecycle, easier rolling, low ops for Acme after initial setup.
- Cons: requires trust to accept cross-signed certs and we need initial KMS wrap/unwrap handoff. OCSP stapling must be provided by Redwood responder that can be validated locally.
- Needs from Acme: one-time CA cross-sign approval, endpoint ACLs, resolver details.

Option B — Customer-managed termination (Acme holds certs):
- Model: Acme provisions certs directly into LB/HSM. Redwood uses mTLS to upstream via an internal service endpoint; cert rotation is controlled by Acme.
- Pros: zero external trust concerns; meets strict KMS/HSM policy.
- Cons: Acme ops owns rotation; risk of mis-rotation causing downtime unless runbook automation is in place.
- Needs from Acme: automation webhook or API to signal rotation events (we can accept S3/KMS push or HashiVault pull).

Option C — Split-termination hybrid (preferred for pilot):
- Model: Short-lived client certs + SNI-based routing to a local TLS proxy (managed by Acme) that forwards to Redwood over an internal private link with mutual TLS using a short-lived session cert issued by your KMS. Redwood provides a responder for OCSP stapling that is reachable via private resolver only.
- Pros: complies with egress policy, keeps long-term CA keys inside your KMS, allows Redwood to manage session certs and provide rollback/fallback.
- Cons: added complexity operationally; requires private DNS entries and an internal route for OCSP responder.
- Needs from Acme: route for OCSP responder (internal ip/name), ability to add short-lived cert issuance webhook or SRV for session cert bootstrap.

Questions for your team (please answer inline):
1) Can the BlueSentinel appliance be configured to allow OCSP stapling from an internal responder hostname?
2) Is there an automation path for issuing short-lived session certs from your KMS (API or signed CSR workflow)?
3) Which option do you favor for the June pilot?

I attached an updated proposal with the option matrix (consolidation_proposal_v1.pdf) — suggests Option C as a low-friction compromise. If you prefer B for strictest controls, we'll prepare a rotation-runbook template.

Thanks,
Ben Carter

Ben / team — thanks for the clear options and for surfacing the OCSP constraint. Quick decision guidance from product/security leadership:

- We should pursue Option C for the June pilot. It best balances Acme's KMS requirements and our ability to provide rollback/fallback during early-stage tests.
- Action items (owners & target dates):
  - Acme SRE (Jake): confirm BlueSentinel config for internal OCSP stapling by 2027-05-24.
  - Karthik: draft a rotation webhook spec (we'll provide a stub implementation) by 2027-05-25.
  - Mina: produce a short security checklist for the pilot (includes audit log requirements, allowed ciphers, TTLs for private zones) by 2027-05-25.

Please treat the checklist as input to the procurement SOW — if Acme signs off on these actions we'll lock the pilot scope and start infra provisioning next week.

Marissa Cole
